analysis.title: Alliance Laundry Holdings Inc. (ALH): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: Alliance reported 3Q adj. EPS of $0.38 vs GS estimate and FactSet consensus of $0.32. The beat came from an adj. EBIT margin of 22.7%, 161bps above the GS model (+$0.03), lower interest expense (+$0.02), and other income and one-time items (+$0.01 each).
Revenue grew 5.3% YOY, modestly below the GS estimate of +6.0% (-$0.01 to EPS).

Management credits local-for-local production, previously announced pricing and tariff refunds with offsetting rising inflation. Commercial in-home and on-premise in North America outperformed, while vended was hurt by project timing.

The midpoint of the 2026 adj. EBITDA guide was raised 1% to +10% YOY, slightly above GS and consensus at +9%. The revenue guide is unchanged at +7% YOY at the midpoint. The raise includes tariff refunds.
North America sales rose 8% YOY vs GSe +7%, on higher volumes in Commercial In-Home and On-Premise. Adj. EBITDA margin expanded ~350bps YOY to 32.4%, 241bps ahead of the GS model.

International revenue fell 1% YOY vs GSe +4%, mainly from FX and project timing in Asia Pacific. Latin America grew solidly and Europe and ME&A were steady. Adj. EBITDA margin rose ~130bps YOY to 25.3% vs GSe 24.6%.
Net debt/EBITDA was 2.3x at end of 3Q, down from 2.4x in 2Q, with $163mn of cash and restricted cash. Management now expects 2.1x by year-end vs 2.0x prior.
Debt paydown of $45mn in the quarter was more than offset by $75mn of repurchases. 2026 capex is maintained at ~3% of sales, or ~$55mn at the midpoint.
GS rates ALH Buy with a $29 12-month price target based on 13.0x its Q5-Q8 EBITDA estimate. The stock closed at $24.04 on 9 Nov 2026, implying 20.6% upside.

Questions for the call: vended upgrade and refresh backlogs, innovation pipeline, commercial in-home demand, international demand given geopolitics, price/cost including steel, and the size of tariff refunds.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q adj. EPS of $0.38 beat the $0.32 consensus on margin strength, and the 2026 adj. EBITDA guide midpoint was raised to +10% YOY. GS keeps its $29 target at 13.0x Q5-Q8 EBITDA.

Higher raw material costs, especially steel, and an inability to pass them through.
Loss of distributors could hurt sales.
Negotiation of the CBA could limit or delay cost reductions and efficiencies.
geopolitical: Geopolitical backdrop produced mixed international results by geography for Alliance.
